citations.assessment: Money spent to demonstrate the high priest’s haircut. The neighboring lines identify his wealth and marriage connection and describe the cut.
Rashi actually says he paid the barber a large sum. It is the remark of the commentary.
The baraita discussion invokes Ben Elasa’s kind of haircut and Rashi describes its close trim.
The witness reads a personal name, Philippos, and says he asked Rabbi Elasa. Equating this figure with Ben Elasa belongs to Heilprin.
Bar Kappara supplies the question and is seen laughing. Rabbi says he does not recognize him as an elder; Bar Kappara understands he will not be appointed in Rabbi’s days.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015
